title: Fabrication of a Bioactive, PCL-based "Self-fitting" Shape Memory Polymer Scaffold
protocol: Run the acrylation reaction.
Weigh 20 g of PCL-diol (Mn = ~10,000 g/mol) into a 250 ml round bottom flask equipped with a Teflon-covered magnetic stir bar.
Dissolve the PCL-diol in DCM by adding 120 mL of DCM to the flask (concentration = 0.17 g/ml).
Stir the solution for ~30 min at ~250 rpm to completely dissolve the polymer.
Add ~6.6 mg of 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) to the solution and dissolve with stirring.
Place a rubber septum securely into the neck of the flask.
Allow the solution to continue stirring.
Gently purge the flask with N2 for ~3 min using a positive N2 pressure needle inlet and an open needle as an outlet.
Remove the N2 inlet and outlet.
Add 0.56 ml (4.0 mmol) of triethylamine (Et3N) dropwise via a glass syringe equipped with a needle inserted through the rubber septum.
Add 0.65 ml (8.0 mmol) of acryloyl chloride dropwise via a glass syringe equipped with a needle inserted through the rubber septum.
Return the N2 inlet to the flask and allow the contents to stir under positive N2 pressure for ~30 min.
Pre-heat an oil bath to 55 ºC.
After the allotted ~30 min, remove the N2 inlet and replace the septum with a condenser.
Submerge the flask into the pre-heated oil bath.
Allow the contents of the flask to stir for 20 hr.
Remove the flask from the oil bath after 20 hours.
Allow the contents to cool to room temperature.
Use a rotary evaporator to remove DCM solvent from the flask.
Add approximately 135 ml of ethyl acetate to the flask and dissolve the crude PCL-DA product.
Gravity filter the solution through filter paper into a clean 250 ml round bottom flask.
If necessary, apply mild heat with a heating gun to facilitate filtration.
Remove ethyl acetate solvent from the flask using a rotary evaporator.
Add approximately 140 ml of DCM to the flask and dissolve the crude PCL-DA.
Transfer contents to a 500 ml separatory funnel.
To the funnel, add 13.5 ml of 2 M potassium carbonate (K2CO3).
Cap the funnel securely.
Invert and gently swirl the funnel once or twice, releasing pressure through the stopcock.
Repeat mixing three times in total.
Replace the cap with a layer of Parafilm and allow the mixture to separate overnight (~12 hours).
Collect the bottom organic layer into a 250 ml Erlenmeyer flask.
Add approximately 5 g of anhydrous magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) to the flask and gently swirl.
Gravity filter the mixture through qualitative filter paper and into a clean 250 ml round bottom flask.
Use a rotary evaporator to remove DCM solvent from the flask.
Dry under high vacuum to remove residual DCM.
Confirm acrylation with 1H NMR.
Use a 425 µm sieve to obtain sodium chloride particles approximately 460 ± 70 µm in diameter.
Add 1.8 g of sieved NaCl to a 3 ml glass vial.
Slowly add, in four portions, 0.146 g of DI water (7.5 wt% based on salt weight) to the vial.
Mix with a metal spatula after the addition of each portion of water.
Cap the vial and wrap it in tissue paper.
Place the capped vial vertically into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 3,220 x g.
Remove the cap from the vial and let air-dry overnight (~12 hours).
Prepare a macromer solution by combining 0.15 g of PCL-DA per ml of DCM in a new glass vial.
Cap and mix the macromer solution at high speed on a vortex mixer for approximately 1 minute.
In a separate new 3 ml glass vial, prepare a photoinitiator solution based on 10 wt% 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenyl acetophenone (DMP) in 1-vinyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NVP).
Combine 0.115 g of DMP with 1 ml of NVP.
Cap the vial containing the photoinitiator solution and wrap it in aluminum foil to block light.
Mix the photoinitiator solution at high speed on a vortex mixer for approximately 1 minute.
If prepared in advance, refrigerate and protect from light the photoinitiator solution.
Wrap the vial containing the macromer solution (excluding the cap) with aluminum foil.
Add via pipette 15 vol% of the photoinitiator solution based on total volume of the macromer solution.
Cap and mix the solution at high speed on a vortex mixer for ~1 min.
Wrap the vial containing the fused salt template (excluding the cap) with aluminum foil.
Add via pipette the previously prepared macromer/photoinitiator solution until the template is completely covered.
Cap the vial, wrap in tissue and place vertically into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 1,260 x g to distribute the macromer solution throughout the template.
Remove the aluminum foil, uncap the vial.
Expose to UV light (365 nm, 25 W) for 3 min.
Air-dry overnight.
Remove the “salt-containing scaffold” from the vial with tweezers after scoring and fracturing the top of the glass vial.
Prepare ~200 ml of a water/ethanol solvent (1:1 vol:vol) in a 400 ml beaker.
Maintain the scaffold submerged in the water/ethanol solvent for 4 days with daily solvent changes.
Remove the scaffold from the solvent and air-dry overnight.
In a 400 ml beaker equipped with a Teflon-covered stir bar, prepare ~200 ml of a dopamine hydrochloride solution (2 mg/ml in 10 mM Tris buffer, pH = 8.5, 25 ºC).
Stir at ~150 rpm.
Place a disposable needle into the scaffold, approximately half the distance through.
Wrap a wire around the needle hub.
Submerge the scaffold with the needle hub above the solution surface in a beaker containing stirring dopamine solution by anchoring the wire to the rim of the beaker.
Degas the scaffold by placing a syringe into the needle hub and pulling air out until no more air can be removed, ensuring complete infiltration of the solution.
Maintain the scaffold submerged for 16 hours.
Remove the scaffold from the dopamine solution and take out the needle.
Rinse the scaffold with DI water.
Dry the scaffold in a vacuum oven at room temperature for 24 hours.
Place the scaffold in an 85 ºC oven for one hour.
Allow the scaffold to cool to room temperature.
Heat DI water to approximately 60 ºC in a beaker.
Place the scaffold into the heated water using tweezers, ensuring all areas are exposed to the water.
Continue submerging the scaffold for about two minutes or until it noticeably softens.
Remove the scaffold from the beaker and immediately press into the model defect by hand.
Allow the scaffold to cool to room temperature (~5-10 min).
Remove the scaffold from the defect to observe its new, fixed temporary shape and return of the relatively more rigid state.
Equilibrate the scaffold to 60 °C for 5 min using a dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA).
Compress the scaffold to a maximum strain of 50 % at 50 %/min.
Hold the scaffold at the maximum strain for 5 min.
Cool the scaffold to 25 °C and maintain for 10 min to fix the temporary shape.
Remove the load from the scaffold.
Measure the ultimate strain in the stress-free state (εu).
Reheat the scaffold to 60 °C and maintain for 10 min to recover the permanent shape.
Measure the recovered strain (εp) after re-heating.
Start the second cycle by compressing the scaffold to 50 % of the height recovered after the first cycle.

Repeat equilibration, compression, holding at maximum strain, cooling, fixing temporary shape, removing load, measuring ultimate strain, reheating, and recovering permanent shape for the second cycle.
Calculate shape fixity (Rf) using the equation Rf(N) = [εu(N)/ εm].
Calculate shape recovery (Rr) using the equation Rr(N) = [εm - εp(N)]/[εm- εp(N-1)].
Observe pore size and pore interconnectivity of the SMP scaffold using scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Submerge the SMP scaffold in liquid N2 for 1 min using tweezers to hold it.
Remove scaffold from liquid N2 and fracture along the middle using a clean razor blade.
Affix one half of the SMP scaffold onto the sample stage with carbon tape, fractured surface facing up.
Sputter coat the affixed scaffold with Au-Pt (~4 nm).
Capture SEM images at an accelerating voltage of 10-15 kV.
Add ~30 ml of 1X SBF to a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Obtain a cylindrical scaffold and cut it in half using a clean blade.
Place one scaffold half into the prepared centrifuge tube and cap.
Maintain the tube at 37 °C in a water bath under static conditions for 14 days.
Remove the scaffold from SBF after 14 days and air dry for 24 hr.
Affix the dried scaffold onto the sample stage with carbon tape, fractured surface facing up.
Sputter coat the affixed scaffold with Au-Pt (~4 nm).
Capture SEM images at an accelerating voltage of 10-15 kV.
